note: Every fixture is a project at some layout state. The skill must resolve the format before it writes anything, hand an old layout to stack-it:migrate rather than restructuring it, and keep generated stack content out of CLAUDE.md in every case. docs/stack.md is a header line, a generated section between <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> markers, and a tail below the end marker that belongs to the user; ownership is decided by the header's '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format N' prefix, since the sentence after it changed between versions. Fixtures with a tail (proj-already-documented, proj-marker-less-0-5-0) pin that the tail survives a regeneration. Fixtures for stop cases (foreign-stack-doc, format-ahead-of-plugin, malformed-stack-doc, lockfile-format-3) hold only the files that trigger the stop, since the skill halts in Step 1 before it reads the stack.

evals.name: from-lockfile
evals.prompt: I want my project's tech stack documented so both my coding agents and new contributors know what we're using and how to run things. Put the agent-facing reference where any agent will find it, and the human-facing part in the README. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Format resolves to 2 off the lockfile's format key, and there is no docs/stack.md, no pointer and no bridge, all three, so this project has never been documented and migrate does not run. Documents from .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml, which validates, with versions matching it exactly. Creates docs/stack.md with the header on line 1, '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.', a blank line, then exactly one <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> pair around the generated section: tools with pinned versions, the real npm build/test/lint/dev commands, the Tailwind-v4-via-Vite-plugin and flat-ESLint conventions (eslint.config.js is present as evidence), and the Vite-7-needs-Node-20.19+ caveat. There is no previous section, so nothing is carried and nothing is superseded, and the report says nothing needed carrying. Creates AGENTS.md with exactly the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md', path NOT in backticks, no HTML markers. Creates CLAUDE.md containing the single line '@AGENTS.md' and no generated stack content. Creates the README with a Tech Stack section + Getting Started inside a <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> managed block with the 'generated/overwritten' note.

evals.name: infer-from-codebase
evals.prompt: There's no stack file for this project. Can you figure out what it's built with and document it? I want a reference my coding agents will pick up, and a tech stack + getting started in the README. If you need me to confirm what you inferred, treat this message as the confirmation and go ahead. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: No docs/stack.md, no lockfile, and no marker block in CLAUDE.md, so there is no format signal at all and nothing to migrate. The stack is inferred from the codebase (pyproject.toml + imports): Python >=3.12, FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0. The package manager is a guess and must be flagged as one: the [dependency-groups] table points at uv or another PEP 735 aware manager, and there is no uv.lock to settle it, so naming uv flatly is wrong. States plainly that the stack was inferred and what it was inferred from; does NOT fabricate a stack.yaml. Creates docs/stack.md with the format 2 header on line 1 and the generated section, including the real run commands (uv run pytest, ruff check, uvicorn app.main:app), inside one marker pair; no tail, nothing carried, nothing superseded. Creates AGENTS.md with the single pointer line, creates CLAUDE.md as the one-line '@AGENTS.md' bridge, and creates the README with its managed block.

evals.name: idempotent-refresh
evals.prompt: The stack changed. Please re-document it. The stack reference and the README section already exist; just bring them up to date. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Both signals read 2, the docs/stack.md header and the lockfile's format key, so migrate must NOT run. The content is STALE: the generated section of docs/stack.md holds old facts (Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.110.0, 'Test: pytest', no uvicorn/Ruff), and the README's <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> block is stale too. Human-written prose lives in AGENTS.md (House rules, Deployment notes), outside the README markers (Contributing), and BELOW the end marker in docs/stack.md (a '## Team notes' section with two lines). Marker integrity runs on docs/stack.md AND the README before either is written. Re-running must (a) replace only what is between the markers in docs/stack.md so it matches the lockfile (FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0, Python 3.14.3), keeping the header line and leaving exactly one marker pair, (b) reproduce the '## Team notes' tail verbatim, same text and same blank lines, on both runs, (c) refresh only what's between the README markers and preserve the prose outside them verbatim, with no second block appended, (d) leave AGENTS.md untouched, since it already contains @docs/stack.md, and leave the one-line '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md alone, (e) put no generated stack content into CLAUDE.md. Every line of the old section is either a superseded version (Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.110.0) or a command the new section restates in the project's own form ('pytest' becomes 'uv run pytest'), so NOTHING is carried: no '## Notes carried forward' heading and no provenance line appear, and no scaffolding from the old section ('# Stack', '## Commands', the bare list bullets) turns up below the end marker either. The report still lists each superseded version and command on its own line, since 'nothing needed carrying' is only said when that list is empty too. Run it twice and the second run produces the same header line, the same tools and versions, the same tail, and no accumulated or duplicated content: its previous section is one this skill just wrote, so every line of it is already stated by the new render and nothing at all is carried. This is the skill's headline idempotency property.

evals.name: agents-md-has-human-rules
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack for the agents and for people, then do it again to check nothing drifts. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The lockfile is stamped format 2, AGENTS.md carries the pointer and CLAUDE.md is the '@AGENTS.md' bridge, but docs/stack.md is missing: the pointer aims at a file that isn't there, which is a missing piece rather than an undocumented project. The skill must INVOKE stack-it:migrate, which writes the stub (header, one marker pair, the single line 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.') so the pointer resolves, and the report must say migrate ran. document-stack then fills the section from the lockfile: the stub line is a migrate marker, so it is dropped rather than carried, and NO stub text survives into the final file. Nothing else was in the section, so nothing is carried. AGENTS.md already holds human-written rules (function components only, co-located tests, second reviewer for src/api/, never commit .env) AND the pointer line. Across two consecutive runs: AGENTS.md ends with exactly ONE 'read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md' line and every human rule verbatim, in its original order, with the pointer still last and still unbackticked. The presence check is on '@docs/stack.md', so the skill appends nothing even though it did not write that sentence itself. docs/stack.md carries the header '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. The section between the markers is regenerated on every run; anything below the end marker is yours and survives.' and on run two only the section between the markers is rewritten: same header line, same tools and versions, no accumulated content, no second marker pair (Vite 7.1.0, React 19.1.0, TypeScript 5.7.3, Tailwind 4.1.11, Vitest 3.2.0, ESLint 9.17.0 with flat config from eslint.config.js). migrate does not run again on the second pass. The one-line '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md is left alone both runs and never receives stack content. The README's managed block is created on run one and refreshed in place on run two, never duplicated.

evals.name: from-v1-layout
evals.prompt: Please re-document this project's stack. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Both readable signals say 1: .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml has no format key, and CLAUDE.md carries the marker block. There is no docs/stack.md, so the highest signal is 1. The skill must INVOKE stack-it:migrate rather than restructuring the layout itself, then continue once migrate reports 'migrated to 2'. End state: no <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> block anywhere in CLAUDE.md; CLAUDE.md starts with '@AGENTS.md' (the user said yes) followed by the House rules and Deployment notes prose intact; stack.yaml stamped 'format: 2' as its first key and still valid; docs/stack.md holding the format 2 header and the section regenerated from the lockfile inside one marker pair (FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0, Python 3.14.3), NOT the stale 0.110.0 text migrate carried in; AGENTS.md carrying the pointer line; the README block refreshed to the uv commands. Anything the carried block said that the new section can't restate belongs below the end marker under '## Notes carried forward'. This block says nothing of the sort: every line is a superseded version (Python 3.12, FastAPI 0.110.0, SQLModel) or the command 'Test: pytest', which the new section restates as 'uv run pytest'. So nothing is carried, no '## Notes carried forward' heading appears, and the report instead lists each superseded version and command on its own line. Carrying the stale 0.110.0 line or the bare 'pytest' command into the tail is one failure this pins; dropping a note with no lockfile field behind it, or letting a superseded version vanish without a report line, are the others. Exactly one layout at the end, never both. The report says migrate ran and what it moved.

evals.name: foreign-stack-doc
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md exists but was written by hand: its first line is '# Our stack, and why', which does not start with '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format', so the file is not ours. The ownership rule must STOP the run there and ask the user before touching the file, showing what's in it. It must NOT go on to use the other signals, which both read 1 (the lockfile has no format key, CLAUDE.md carries a marker block) and would start a migration. Nothing is written: docs/stack.md is not overwritten, no markers are inserted into it, the CLAUDE.md block is still there with the House rules and Deployment notes around it, no AGENTS.md is created, no README is created. A cut CLAUDE.md block is the visible sign of the failure this pins, which is clobbering a human's hand-maintained stack document.

evals.name: format-ahead-of-plugin
evals.prompt: Bring the stack docs up to date for the project at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md carries a valid generated header reading 'format 3' while .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml says 'format: 2'. Reading every signal and taking the highest gives 3, which is ahead of the current format 2, so the skill stops and writes nothing and tells the user a newer stack-it wrote this project and the plugin should be upgraded. It must not downgrade the file, not overwrite docs/stack.md or the section inside its markers, and not settle on the lockfile's 2 because it looks current. migrate is not invoked.

evals.name: recorded-decline-not-reasked
evals.prompt: Re-document the stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR, then run it once more.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md holds the user's own prose plus the pointer line, the recorded fallback from a run where they declined the '@AGENTS.md' import. AGENTS.md is the pointer-only file stack-it created. Across two runs the skill must NOT ask about the import again: the 'already contains @docs/stack.md outside backticks' case matches before the ask, so CLAUDE.md is left alone both times, with no '@AGENTS.md' line added and no second pointer line appended. docs/stack.md keeps its header and has only the section between its markers refreshed from the lockfile. The old section is sorted line by line: 'Python 3.12' and 'FastAPI 0.110.0' are superseded versions and 'Test: pytest' is a command the new section restates as 'uv run pytest', so those three are dropped and reported; 'SQLModel 0.0.22' matches the lockfile, so it is set aside and not reported. NONE of the four may appear below the end marker. The '## Gotchas' line about the lifespan handler creating the SQLite tables has no lockfile field behind it, so it is carried below the end marker under '## Notes carried forward' and listed in the report. Nothing else is carried: the '## Gotchas' heading above it is scaffolding the new section restates in its own form, so the heading stays out of the tail and only the note itself moves. The heading is created with exactly one provenance line under it, 'Carried forward by stack-it. Each line says something the generated section above did not; prune what the section grows to cover.', undated so it is byte-stable. The second run must not duplicate that note or that line and must carry nothing new, and AGENTS.md and the README block are refreshed or left alone as usual.

evals.name: hand-tuned-block-survives
evals.prompt: Re-document this project's stack. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. Then run it once more. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: A format 1 project: the lockfile has no format key and CLAUDE.md carries the marker block, so migrate runs first. The block is not a plain render of the lockfile. Besides the tools list it holds three notes across four bullet lines that no lockfile field can express: the pnpm hoisting gotcha ('pnpm does not hoist. A package you import but never list in package.json resolves in local dev and fails at runtime on the build box; add it explicitly'), the Turbopack note ('serves stale CSS after renaming a module. Restart the dev server; a hard refresh does not clear it'), and the 'Built / pending' ledger (built: orders list, order detail, CSV export; pending: bulk refunds, audit log view, Stripe webhook replay). migrate must CARRY the whole block into docs/stack.md under the placeholder line 'Moved from CLAUDE.md by migrate; run document-stack to regenerate.' inside the markers, even though a valid lockfile exists: dropping it because the lockfile can regenerate the tools is the 0.5.0 bug this eval exists for. migrate writes docs/stack.md BEFORE it cuts the block, so a failure between the two leaves a duplicate rather than a hole. document-stack then regenerates the section from the lockfile and the codebase only (Node.js 22.14.0, pnpm 10.4.1, Next.js 15.2.0, React 19.0.0, TypeScript 5.7.3, Tailwind CSS 4.0.9, Vitest 3.0.7, ESLint 9.21.0) and moves all three notes below the end marker under a '## Notes carried forward' heading, with exactly one provenance line under the heading ('Carried forward by stack-it. Each line says something the generated section above did not; prune what the section grows to cover.'), and lists each note in the report so the user can prune it. The report also names any carried note the new section has grown to cover, as a prune candidate, and never edits the tail itself. The placeholder line is a migrate marker: dropped, never carried into the tail. The stale 'Next.js 15.1.0' pin does NOT survive anywhere, since it is a version the lockfile supersedes, and the report says so on its own line. End state: docs/stack.md has the header on line 1, exactly one marker pair, the regenerated section inside it and the three notes below it; CLAUDE.md is '@AGENTS.md' followed by the rest of the file (title, House rules, Deployment notes) byte for byte; AGENTS.md carries the pointer; stack.yaml is stamped 'format: 2'. Nothing a human typed was lost. The second run replaces the section again, leaves the tail alone, and carries nothing new: by then the previous section is this skill's own output, so every line of it is already stated by the new render. No heading from the section ('# Stack', '## Commands', '## Gotchas') ever appears under '## Notes carried forward'; scaffolding is set aside, not carried. The second run reuses the existing heading and provenance line rather than writing a second of either.

evals.name: marker-less-0-5-0
evals.prompt: Re-document this project's stack. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md was written by stack-it 0.5.0: its first line is '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. Edits are overwritten on the next run.', the OLD trailing sentence. Ownership is decided by the '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format N' prefix, so this file IS ours; reading it as somebody else's and stopping is one failure this pins. The lockfile is stamped 2 and the layout is complete, so migrate does not run. The file has no markers, so the entire body below the header is the old generated section and every line of it goes through the carry-forward: nothing in that file says where the generated text stopped, so the hand-added '## Team notes' section (staging behind the shared nginx box, scripts/seed.py truncating first) is carried like any other text rather than guessed at. End state: the header rewritten to the new sentence, exactly one marker pair added around the section regenerated from the lockfile (Python 3.14.3, uv 0.6.12, FastAPI 0.115.0, uvicorn 0.34.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0), and below the end marker a '## Notes carried forward' heading, one provenance line under it, and then the uvicorn --reload watcher gotcha and both Team notes lines. The old '# Stack', '## Commands', '## Gotchas' and '## Team notes' headings are scaffolding, so they do not come along; the lines under them do. The stale Python 3.12 and FastAPI 0.110.0 lines and the bare 'pytest' command are superseded, so they are dropped and reported, never carried into the tail. The report says the markers were added, and the format stays 2 with no bump.

evals.name: from-migrate-stub
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The lockfile has no format key and there is nothing else to read: no docs/stack.md, no CLAUDE.md, no AGENTS.md. A missing key reads as 1, so the project is behind and stack-it:migrate is invoked. migrate stamps 'format: 2', finds no block to move, and writes the stub docs/stack.md: header, one marker pair, and the single line 'Placeholder written by migrate; run document-stack to fill this in.' It also creates the pointer and the '@AGENTS.md' bridge, then reports 'migrated to 2'. document-stack carries on and fills the section from the lockfile (Python 3.14.3, uv 0.6.12, FastAPI 0.115.0, uvicorn 0.34.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0) with the real uv commands. The stub line is one of the two migrate markers, so it is dropped rather than carried: it must appear nowhere in the final file, above or below the end marker, and no '## Notes carried forward' heading is created, because there was nothing else in the section. The report says migrate ran, what it wrote, and that nothing needed carrying. The README gets its managed block.

evals.name: malformed-stack-doc
evals.prompt: Re-document the stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md is ours, its header prefix is right, and it holds a '<!-- stack-it:stack start -->' with NO matching end marker, so where the generated section stops is unknowable. Marker integrity fails and the skill writes NOTHING, anywhere: docs/stack.md is untouched, no README is created, no AGENTS.md, no CLAUDE.md. It shows the user the offending lines and stops. Two failures this pins: guessing where the section ends and replacing to end of file, which would eat the '## Team notes' lines below; and running the check late, after docs/stack.md or the README had already been written.

evals.name: lockfile-format-3
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: The mirror of format-ahead-of-plugin: .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml is stamped 'format: 3' while docs/stack.md still carries a valid format 2 header. Every signal is read and the highest wins, so the format is 3, ahead of the current 2. The skill stops and writes nothing, and tells the user a newer stack-it wrote this project and the plugin should be upgraded. Settling on the docs/stack.md header because it reads 2, or refreshing the section under it, is the failure this pins. migrate is not invoked, and neither file is rewritten or downgraded.
